teaser: 551 of 566 links between articles point back in time. Why older articles should say what came next and what corrected them.
core_idea: Links between articles are written when an article is written, so almost all point back in time; the site derives a Continued by list at each article's foot, but it is easy to miss and does not separate a sequel from a correction, so older articles should carry typed forward links, what came next, corrected by and status since, at the top, added in turns from the newest articles down.

quotes.text: A forward link to a sequel is a convenience. A forward link to a correction is the record.
quotes.why: Why corrections matter more than sequels.

quotes.text: When I write in sequence, the later piece usually says so; the earlier piece almost never learns.
